- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from prior 30d mean), model overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above peak.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model fails to mean-revert; apply smoothing filter to forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 30d mean is 72.5, price drops to 70.0), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- For 30d horizon, if model forecast is >75% above 30d mean, flag as overconfident; adjust downward by 5–10% unless sentiment supports.
- If sentiment history shows recent negative sentiment (e.g., 3 consecutive low values), model often ignores it; reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect pessimism.
